title: Thou Must Be Born Again
description: Thou Must Be Born Again in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Johns wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 200, “Thou Must Be Born Again”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thou must be born a-gain! Such was the sol-emn word To him who came, not all in vain, By night to seek his Lord.

lines: To him who came, not all in vain,
By night to seek his Lord.
But not the birth of clay;
The immortal seed must thence obtain
Must move and guide thy soul.
Thou canst not choose but trace
If once thou feel his truth and grace,
Seek well and thou shalt find at last

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Johns died in 1847.
credits: Words by John Johns (1801–1847), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
